April 10, 2025
Testimony in Favor of L.D. 988, "An Act to Allow Hunting on University of Maine System Property", before the Committee On Education and Cultural Affairs, presented by David Trahan, Executive Director, Sportsman's Alliance of Maine Institute for Legislative Action.
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs,
My name is David Trahan. I am the Executive Director for Sportsman's Alliance of Maine Institute for Legislative Action and I am testifying today in support of a resolution to the issue raised in L.D. 988, An Act to Allow Hunting on University of Maine Property.
The Sportsman's Alliance of Maine Institute for Legislative Action would like to thank Senator Timberlake for sponsoring L.D. 988. We would also like to thank Samantha Warren, Chief External & Governmental Affairs Officer for the University of Maine. Given the sometime controversial nature of hunting and public access, Ms. Warren has conducted herself at the highest levels of professionalism.
When it was made public last year that the University would no longer allow hunting on their nearly 15,000 acres, both sides of the issue could have gone to their corners and hunkered down for a fight. They did not. Instead, a positive back and forth has led to significant progress toward a policy solution.

In discussions with the University and the sponsor of the bill, it is clear there could be a final hunting policy before the next hunting season, that strikes a balance between safety and wildlife management, that is acceptable to all.
We anticipate continued positive talks and feel it is likely this bill will be unnecessary. With that thought in mind, we hope the committee will hold this bill over until next legislative session and allow the policy to be finished and presented to the committee, sponsor and our organization for review, so we can assist to educate the public about the new conditions.
Again, thank you to the Senator Timberlake and Samantha Warren.
David Trahan, Executive Director Sportsman's Alliance of Maine Institute for Legislative Action 205 Church Hill Road, Suite 3 Augusta, ME 04330 david@samofmaine.org 207-623-4589

LD 988, "An Act to Allow Hunting on University of Maine System Property"
Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs April 10, 2025

Senator Rafferty, Representative Noonan Murphy, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs:
My name is Senator Jeff Timberlake, and I represent Senate District 17. I`m here today to introduce LD 988, "An Act to Allow Hunting on University of Maine System Property," which would allow
for hunting on certain areas of University of Maine System land, with the exception of residential areas and campus zones.
Currently, the blanket restriction on hunting and weapons across University of Maine properties unintentionally limits wildlife management practices that are important for the health of these lands.
As we all know, overpopulation of deer and other wildlife can lead to a number of problems, like the spread of disease, an increase in ticks, and damage to the surrounding environment. Left
umnanaged, these issues can quickly escalate, causing harm to our ecosystems.
I want to be clear, the intent here isn't to challenge the broader policies around weapons on campus, which are based on ensuring public safety. However, it's important to acknowledge that these lands can suffer from the same ecological challenges that private lands face; and they require the correct
management. By allowing hunting on certain University of Maine System properties, we can help
control wildlife populations and prevent the negative effects that come with overpopulation, all
while keeping safety at the forefront.
This bill would specifically allow hunting on non-residential areas of University of Maine System property, keeping it far from places where students and faculty are. It's a practical way to balance the need for wildlife management with the safety and well-being of students and faculty.
Supporting this bill would not only help preserve the health of Maine's ecosystems, but also offer more opportunities for hunting, which is a key part of our outdoor traditions here in Maine. I ask for your support in moving this bill forward,
Thank you for your time and consideration.

UNIVERSITY OF MAINE SYSTEM

University of Maine System Testimony in Opposition to LD 988, An Act to Allow Hunting on University of Maine System Property -- Presented by UMS Chief External
& Governmental Affairs Officer Samantha Warren --- April 10, 2025
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Education & Cultural Affairs: My name is Sam Warren and I am the Chief External & Governmental Affairs Officer for the University of Maine System (UMS).
Our System has a strong tradition of supporting the North American model of wildlife conservation, of which hunting is foundational, through our tripartite mission of teaching, research, and service. For example, at our University of Maine Cooperative Extension 4-H Camps and Learning Centers, we partner with the Maine Department of Inland Fisheries & Wildlife (MDIFW) to provide hunter safety courses and certification to hundreds of Maine youth each year. UMaine research also informs the State's management of key wildlife populations and our System prepares Maine's wildlife conservation workforce, including many of MDlFW's wildlife biologists and game wardens. Legislative appropriations for UMS, which have long not kept pace with inflation, will be essential to our ability to
sustain and strengthen these vital programs and sen/ices for Maine in the future.
As part of our recognition of Maine's hunting tradition and consistent with our public mission, UMaine has long allowed hunting on thousands of acres of the forest land
we directly own or manage. However, last fall, the university became aware that a dozen
individuals had been told they could hunt on university research farms by those not formally authorized to grant that permission. Students, faculty, staff, and external partners are actively using these properties for research and extension necessary to the success and sustainability of the livestock and dairy farmers, tree fruit and vegetable growers, wild blueberry producers, and potato processors in your districts and throughout Maine. At the
time, we publicly acknowledged that our employees and the members of the public who sought hunting access did so in good faith and we clarified that the research farms, which
collectively comprise about 1,200 acres and are located in Jonesboro, Monmouth, Old Town, Orono and Presque Isle, were not open to hunting.
The questions and concerns raised as a result led the university to convene a group to draft an official policy for hunting on our property. That policy, which remains under development, will balance the need for our researchers and partners to safely engage in education, research, and extension activities on university-owned and managed property while also promoting equitable public access to more than 10,000 acres of our land, including for
hunflng.
When that policy is finalized before the fall hunting season, I am happy to provide a copy to this Committee, which may wish to carry over this bill until then. Our policy will also be
